expert_diagnosis: Supertech suffered a classic real-estate developer insolvency driven by cash-flow mismatch between project collections and delivery obligations, accumulated lender debt without project-level ring-fencing, and progressive homebuyer trust collapse. The Rs 432+ crore default to Union Bank of India was the triggering legal event but underlying causes were structural: overextension, insufficient project-level financial controls, and inability to complete projects once sales velocity slowed.
expert_first_action: Ring-fence all remaining project cash flows on a project-by-project basis, prioritize completion of most-advanced projects to restore credibility, and engage lenders and homebuyers in a coordinated standstill while preparing a verified completion plan.
actual_decision: NCLT admitted the insolvency petition filed by Union Bank of India on 25 March 2022, initiating the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) for Supertech Ltd.
harmful_actions: Failure to ring-fence project-level cash flows allowed cross-subsidization and cash leakage
Continued new project launches while existing projects were stalled depleted available resources
Failure to engage lenders and homebuyers in structured standstill before legal escalation
Governance failure to install independent project-level fund monitoring
beneficial_actions: NCLT-led insolvency process provided a formal framework for homebuyer and creditor claims
Later proceedings involved NCLAT and Supreme Court consideration of homebuyer protection
Alternative completion arrangements were explored through the CIRP process
citation: Supertech Limited official public announcement page confirming NCLT insolvency order. The Legal School blog on Supertech insolvency and NCLT proceedings. Supreme Court order records.
actual_outcome: NCLT admitted insolvency petition on 25 March 2022. CIRP initiated. Homebuyer claims, project completion concerns, NCLAT and Supreme Court proceedings followed. Alternative developer and completion arrangements were explored but homebuyer delivery remained significantly impaired.
documented_root_causes: Project cash-flow mismatch between collections and delivery obligations
Debt accumulation and default to lenders
Delivery execution failure across multiple projects
Governance failure in project-level fund ring-fencing
Real-estate working-capital stress from sector slowdown
final_business_state: Under CIRP per NCLT order of 25 March 2022. Homebuyer delivery significantly impaired. Ongoing legal proceedings across NCLT, NCLAT, and Supreme Court for project completion and creditor resolution.
